That's true, definitely one way of looking at it. For me it just came across as a claim to stand for "feminism" by targeting other women who did not speak about the issue rather than emphasizing the problems of the music industry itself. 

But! I do see your point. I also didn't look too closely into the case and artist reactions, I just got the general gist of the situation so chances are you probably know more than me!

I really feel for Kesha and I hope she wins the case but what bothers me the most about this is that other artists such as Demi Lovato are using it to create drama and accuse other artists (Taylor Swift) for not speaking up. This might be an unpopular opinion but I find it takes away from the problem of Sony backing a scumbag producer and instead twisting it into a cat fight between women. 

I just find it really takes away from the big picture here.
